title: QB1_A#q27 taught India's cargo regime as the repealed COGSA 1925 with Hague-Visby by contract only
candidate_claim: Raised by production. Writing the Hamburg Rules card (H7-002, for SEP-0135) required the India limb, and the adjacent Hague-Visby card still taught 'India ratified the Hague Rules 1924 through the Carriage of Goods by Sea Act 1925' and an India-ratification trap built on it.
rationale: The Carriage of Goods by Sea Act, 2025 (Act No. 19 of 2025, assent 8 Aug 2025) repeals the 1925 Act (s.12(1)); its preamble recites the 1924 rules as amended by the Protocols of 23 Feb 1968 and 21 Dec 1979, and its Schedule carries 666.67 SDR per package or 2 SDR per kg. Hague-Visby therefore applies in India by statute. The card's Indian Application paragraph, 60-second answer, reg-box row, India trap, Numbers line and version stamp are corrected; a candidate would otherwise contradict the new Hamburg card and the statute. Treaty accession to the Protocols is NOT asserted - not established by the sources held.
note: A repair to a shipped card found during H7 production gets its own record (tools/oral/SKILL.md 8.2); it is not back-dated into the batch.
authority: Gazette of India Extraordinary, CG-DL-E-09082025-265333 (Act No. 19 of 2025), read 2026-09-23; commencement S.O. 4082(E) of 8 Sep 2025 appointing 10 Sep 2025 confirmed only from secondary sources and registered for recheck. Registered as SRC-INDIA-COGSA-2025.
propagation: Swept all 86 question-bearing files on 2026-09-23 for 'COGSA', 'Carriage of Goods by Sea Act' and 'Hague Rules 1924 through'. Outside QB1_A only two generic mentions exist - QB8_B#q3 reg-box 'COGSA (Carriage of Goods by Sea Act) - Electronic Provisions' and QB9_H 'Indian Bills of Lading law / COGSA framework' - neither names the 1925 Act or its content, so neither is corrected. On QB1_A every remaining '1925' is negated ('repealed') or quoted as the trap, per SKILL.md 8.2a.
